label: prop:habiro-precision-ladder-equivalence
title: Precision-ladder coefficients are Habiro integer evaluations
html:
Proposition. Precision-ladder coefficients are Habiro integer evaluations

The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q) of any braid word admits a finite Habiro expansion with integer coefficients a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[u]. The Habiro form is the canonical representation: it is an exact, finite rational evaluation, not a truncated series.

Specifically, the Markov trace of the neutron–proton braid-word difference admits the finite expansion

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_n) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{m=0}^{M} a_m(u) \cdot (u;\,u)_m,
  \qquad
  a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[u],

where u = q^{1/2}, (u;\,u)_m = \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1-u^{k}) is the q-Pochhammer symbol, and M < \infty (the series terminates).

Under the archimedean evaluation u \mapsto u_0 at the substrate square-root, each (u_0;\,u_0)_m contributes a factor that shrinks like \sim \hbar_q^m, where \hbar_q is the universal substrate Planck quantum (categorical; the exact algebraic values at the substrate q_0 are not reproduced here).

The verified proton Habiro coefficients, the uniqueness of the archimedean evaluation, and the scope of the exact evaluation are collected in the Habiro precision-ladder context.

Archimedean specialisation. The Habiro / precision-ladder Taylor coefficients (\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}) are the real archimedean evaluations of the generic Habiro-ring expansion; the real coefficient sequences sit on the archimedean side of the substrate wall, acknowledged here.
